experiment_name: Pure PPO (hybrid=False) BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE learnability gate: 32-game training, player_id=0 vs FPAgentA/B/C, corrected-state pipeline

environment_gate.problem: The prior session's Python interpreter (AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312) had numpy.random/_mt19937 blocked by a local Application Control policy - unrelated to this project's code, but blocking any np.random.default_rng() call.
environment_gate.resolution: Found an existing, already-set-up project interpreter at C:\mpvenv\Scripts\python.exe (numpy 2.5.2, torch 2.13.0+cpu, pytest 9.1.1) with fully working numpy.random and a clean full project test suite (616 passed before this run's own additions, 635 after) - no environment changes, no new installs, no security-policy changes made.

algorithm_config.opponents: FPAgentA/FPAgentB/FPAgentC (monopoly_game_engine.agents_fixed, reference, unmodified) - hardcoded inside train()'s own opponent pool, not overridden
algorithm_config.seed_scheme: one base seed (45000) passed to train(); train() derives episode_seed = base + game_index deterministically for games 1..32 (its own unmodified logic) - all 32 derived seeds pre-registered as DEV pool 45000-45031 in scripts/evaluation_protocol.py before this run, validated via evaluation_protocol.require_seed_scope before any training happened
algorithm_config.why_hybrid_false: Every prior BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE finding in this project (023/024/025/026) measured a checkpoint whose actor was bootstrapped from a HYBRID PPO run where these two actions were always fixed-ruled and therefore never received a PPO gradient update at all (023's core finding). This run asks the more basic prerequisite question: with hybrid=False from the start (both actions fully neural, agent_ppo.py's fixed_action_mask entirely False), does PPO gradient descent move them at all?
algorithm_config.state_pipeline: monopolyzero_common.ensure_reference_on_path() called before any reference import - installs the actor-relative property-owner encoding patch (see docs/DECISIONS.md's 2026-08-12 entry) so training and the diagnostic read share one consistent state pipeline. player_id=0's own live game states are provably unaffected by that fix either way (actor_order(0) is the identity ordering) - this is about pipeline consistency, not a live correctness requirement for this specific learner.
algorithm_config.asu_involvement: none - zero ASU imports anywhere in this run's import chain (agent_ppo.py, train.py, networks.py, agents_fixed.py, env.py, state.py, actions.py, constants.py all independently grepped clean of "asu"/"ASU"; common.loaded_asu_modules() also checked at runtime and returned empty)
algorithm_config.mcts_involvement: none - pure single-forward-pass PPO action selection (ActorNetwork.get_action), no search, no MaxNPUCT, no MCTS visit targets anywhere in this run

diagnostic_set.source: experiment 026's 55,215-position replay, filtered to actor_id==0 ONLY (13,961 positions)
diagnostic_set.why_026_is_safe_here_despite_being_pre_f: 026 is PRE-FIX diagnostic-only data for TRAINING purposes (both its stored states and its MCTS visit targets used the old, pre-owner-encoding-fix physical-id ownership indexing for actor_id 1-3). This run never trains on 026 - it is used ONLY as a static, read-only set of realistic board positions for masked forward-pass measurement. Critically, actor_id==0's state encoding is byte-for-byte IDENTICAL before and after the owner-encoding fix (actor_order(0) == (0,1,2,3), the identity ordering the bug coincidentally already produced for physical id 0 - proven by tests/test_monopolyzero_actor_relative_owner_fix.py::test_agent_id_zero_encoding_byte_for_byte_unchanged_by_fix), so the actor_id==0 subset used here is unaffected by which side of the fix 026 was generated on.

instrumentation.instrument_agent: wraps the PPOAgent instance's own bound choose_action/store methods (new instance attributes, reference PPOAgent class untouched) to record real runtime data: whether BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE were ever excluded from the neural candidate set when legal, and how many times each was actually stored into a PPO transition (which agent_ppo.py's own Bug-1 fix guarantees only happens with a non-None log_prob)
instrumentation.install_fallback_counting_fixed_agents: monkeypatches monopoly_game_engine.train's own FPAgentA/FPAgentB/FPAgentC module-global bindings (not the reference classes) to subclasses that additionally count when train.py's own run_episode had to substitute the fixed opponent's proposed action - the vanilla reference train() does not expose this number on its own. Restored immediately after the run.

algorithm_config.pre_registered_decision_rule: GO to a real strength A/B only if: (1) BUY and ACCEPT output rows both actually changed; (2) neither action is structurally excluded from neural training; (3) held-out mean prior rank improves for BOTH BUY and ACCEPT overall; (4) improvement direction occurs in a majority of available held-out game_id blocks for BOTH actions; (5) no integrity failure, ASU use, illegal action, or crash. Otherwise KILL PPO scaling for now. Registered before this run was executed.

item3_mean_prior_rank_improves_both_over.note: BUY_PROPERTY improved sharply; ACCEPT_TRADE regressed - item 3 requires BOTH, so this item fails on ACCEPT_TRADE alone

item4_majority_of_game_id_blocks_improve.note: BUY_PROPERTY improved in 8/8 held-out game_id blocks (unanimous). ACCEPT_TRADE improved in 0/8 (unanimous regression, not a marginal/ambiguous split) - item 4 fails on ACCEPT_TRADE alone

item5_no_integrity_failure.opponent_fallback_note: This is the reference train()'s own long-standing silent-substitution behavior for scripted fixed opponents (FPAgentA/B/C proposing something momentarily illegal, substituted with END_TURN/allowed[0] by train.py's own run_episode) - present regardless of hybrid mode or this gate's own code, and not an ASU/illegal-action/crash event for the PPO learner under test. Not previously measured by the vanilla reference train() (unlike monopoly_bench.play_local_game's fallback_count) - measured here for the first time via install_fallback_counting_fixed_agents.

algorithm_config.overall_verdict: KILL PPO scaling for now (items 3 and 4 both fail, cleanly and unanimously, on ACCEPT_TRADE specifically - not a marginal or ambiguous result). No training loss was reinterpreted as success.

metrics.note: Full per-game_id (43000-43007) before/after breakdown is in the raw JSON payload referenced in raw_logs, not duplicated here.

result: PURE PPO (hybrid=False) learnability gate over 32 games: BUY_PROPERTY moved sharply and consistently toward being learnable (mean legal-action rank 5.57->1.20 overall, improved in all 8/8 held-out game_id blocks, greedy-choice rate 1.8%->81.5%) - a real, structural, non-null-log_prob neural signal, unlike every prior hybrid-bootstrapped checkpoint measured in this project. ACCEPT_TRADE moved the opposite direction (mean rank 2.51->5.11 overall, regressed in all 8/8 held-out game_id blocks, greedy-choice rate 63.7%->55.2%), despite also being fully neural (0 structural exclusions) and its output row also genuinely changing. Both output rows changed, neither action was structurally excluded, zero ASU/crashes/illegal actions from the learning agent, all 32 games completed. Per the pre-registered decision rule (GO requires items 1-5 ALL true), items 3 and 4 fail because they require improvement for BOTH actions and ACCEPT_TRADE regressed unanimously - verdict is KILL for scaling this exact PPO recipe as a blanket direction, not GO to a strength A/B. This is not reinterpreted as a loss-curve success claim (no loss was even captured - see the loss field). The BUY_PROPERTY-vs-ACCEPT_TRADE asymmetry itself is a genuine, non-obvious finding worth carrying forward, but root-causing it (reward shaping, opponent trade-behavior distribution, action-space size difference) is out of scope for this gate.
notes: loss is null: the reference train()'s own history dict does not aggregate per-update actor_loss/critic_loss/entropy into its returned history (run_episode receives them from PPOAgent.update() but train() never stores result['stats'] into history) - this gate did not add extra instrumentation to capture them, since the task's own decision rule is explicitly about held-out prior-rank movement and structural change proof, not loss. Checkpoint (~a few MB) is not committed per CLAUDE.md - referenced by SHA-256 and local path only.
